The house
A house that breathes.
Completed in 2025 in the Laurie Baker tradition, this home is built of exposed wire-cut brick — no paint or plaster to maintain, and naturally cool rooms through the Tirunelveli summer. Jali screens pull daylight and breeze through every floor, and filler-slab ceilings of clay tile reduce both heat and material.
Two floors hold a 2 BHK home of 1,300 sq ft on a 1,600 sq ft east-facing plot, with Mangalore-tiled verandahs, a covered carport for car and bike, and a rooftop terrace over open paddy fields.

Highlights
Natural exposed brick
Wire-cut brick walls with no paint or plaster to maintain — and naturally cool interiors year-round.
Jali ventilation
Perforated brick screens draw daylight and cross-breeze through the house without letting the heat in.
Rooftop terrace
Brick-paved terrace with parapet railing and open views over the paddy fields behind the house.
Filler-slab ceilings
Clay tiles set into the concrete slabs — a Baker signature that keeps rooms cooler using less concrete.
Covered parking
Mangalore-tiled carport with sheltered space for a car and a bike, behind designer metal gates.
Farmland views
Quiet residential street in front, open green paddy fields behind — town convenience, village calm.
